recent_posts.title: New Mentoring Team with Experienced Mentors and New Voices
recent_posts.summary: rOpenSci has announced the eleven mentors for its 2026 Champions Program. The team includes two new mentors (Alber Sánchez Ipia and Pablo Paccioretti), three former Champions now serving as mentors (Erick Navarro Delgado, Guadalupe Pascal, Andrea Gomez Vargas, and Monika Avila Marquez), and returning experienced mentors from previous cohorts. The group spans multiple countries and disciplines, with strong representation from Latin America. Mentors will guide new Champions in developing R packages and growing as open science leaders. The Champions selection is complete and will be announced soon.

recent_posts.title: Differential Machine Learning with Twin Networks in R: Forecasting Bitcoin with Volatility Proxies
recent_posts.summary: Differential Machine Learning (DML) is adapted for Bitcoin price forecasting in R using a twin-network architecture built with Keras3. Instead of mathematical derivatives, RSI, MACD, and Bollinger Bands serve as volatility proxies. A primary network learns price/trend dynamics while an auxiliary network captures volatility signals. Their outputs are combined via a linear regression stacking ensemble, reducing RMSE from ~76,000 (individual networks) to ~3,030 and MAPE from ~99% to ~3.65%. Residual-based 95% confidence intervals are added for uncertainty quantification, and results are visualized with ggplot2.

recent_posts.title: Setting function parameters for debugging
recent_posts.summary: A practical R utility function called `set_function_params()` that automates the tedious process of setting function parameters in the global environment for interactive debugging. When debugging R functions with many parameters, developers normally have to manually assign each default value. This function uses `formals()` to extract all parameters from a given function and assigns their default values to a specified environment (global by default), returning a data frame showing which parameters were set and their values. The post demonstrates its use on a 23-parameter plotting function from the `clav` package.

recent_posts.title: JAGS 5.0.0-beta is available
recent_posts.summary: JAGS 5.0.0-beta is now available on SourceForge. The beta targets R package authors who depend on JAGS interfaces (rjags, runjags, R2jags, jagsUI) and early adopters willing to test before the official release. Source tarballs and binaries for Windows and macOS (x86_64 and arm64) are provided. The companion rjags_5-1 package is also available but not yet on CRAN due to reverse dependency issues. Feedback can be submitted via the JAGS forums or as bug reports.

recent_posts.title: Comparing R’s {targets} and dbt for Data Engineering
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on comparison of R's {targets} package and dbt (data build tool) for building a personal finance data pipeline. The author builds a 'slowbooks' workflow that ingests bank CSV exports, stages and cleans transactions, joins with merchant categories, produces monthly aggregations, and runs data validation tests. Both tools are implemented side-by-side across staging, intermediate, and mart layers, with dbt using SQL/Jinja models backed by DuckDB and {targets} using R/dplyr/fuzzyjoin. Key differences highlighted include dbt's SQL-centric approach with built-in test framework versus {targets}' R-native flexibility with third-party validation packages like {data.validator}. The author notes dbt suits SQL-first data teams while {targets} better serves R users who prefer programmatic abstractions.

recent_posts.title: The Magic of In-Context Learning (ICL): When Your Model Already Knows Your Data
recent_posts.summary: In-Context Learning (ICL) allows pre-trained models to make predictions on new data without any retraining. The TabPFN R package brings this capability to tabular data by applying a Transformer architecture — the same used in LLMs — to spreadsheet rows instead of text tokens. Rather than training on real-world datasets, TabPFN was trained on millions of synthetically generated mathematical dependency structures, giving it broad pattern recognition for tabular data. A demo using the iris dataset achieves 97.8% accuracy with no hyperparameter tuning, positioning TabPFN as a compelling alternative to Random Forests or XGBoost for small to medium datasets.

recent_posts.title: Bad Weather and the Subway
recent_posts.summary: An analysis of NYC Subway hourly ridership data from 2025 compared against National Weather Service severe weather events. By plotting ridership profiles for bad weather days against typical day-of-week baselines, four patterns emerge: weather events with no impact on ridership, suppressed ridership due to non-weather factors (e.g., day after Christmas), genuine weather-driven travel suppression (e.g., flash flooding), and a surprising fourth case where the first snowfall of the season actually increased weekend subway ridership as New Yorkers went out to enjoy the snow.

recent_posts.title: Regression Modeling Strategies Short Course 2026, with Frank Harrell; May 14, 15, 18, 19
recent_posts.summary: Frank Harrell's Regression Modeling Strategies online short course is scheduled for May 14, 15, 18, and 19, 2026. The four-day workshop covers building, validating, and interpreting multivariable regression models, with topics including spline methods, data reduction, Bayesian modeling, semiparametric ordinal and survival models, and resampling-based validation. Examples are illustrated using R and the rms package. The course is offered through Instats in association with the ASA.

recent_posts.title: Reactive Shiny Apps and Deployment with Google Cloud Run: Intermediate R Shiny Workshop
recent_posts.summary: An intermediate R Shiny workshop announcement covering reactive programming patterns, app structure, and deployment to Google Cloud Run. The session is part of the Workshops for Ukraine series, scheduled for May 21st, and targets developers who already know Shiny basics and want to build more robust, maintainable apps. Registration requires a minimum donation of 20 EUR, with all proceeds supporting Ukraine.

recent_posts.title: rOpenSci News Digest, April 2026
recent_posts.summary: The April 2026 rOpenSci monthly digest covers community news including the passing of R-Core member Tomáš Kalibera, two new editors joining the review team, and a new Champions Program cohort. On the software side, the reviser package for time series revision analysis was added to the suite, and ten packages received updates. The digest also highlights a Bioconductor and R-universe infrastructure collaboration, updates to the goodpractice package, tree-sitter tooling for R, tips on R package development (Jarl CLI, lintr, random seeds, coalesce operator), and calls for package maintainers.

top_posts.title: Tabler 0.1.0 is here!
top_posts.summary: Tabler 0.1.0 is a new dashboard framework for R Shiny built on the Tabler Dashboard design system. Released under Apache 2.0 license, it offers 13 different layout options including boxed, combo, fluid, vertical, and RTL modes, with customizable themes and colors. The package provides flexibility for creating modern dashboards with sidebar navigation, top navbars, and various styling options. Installation is available through R-Universe or GitHub, with comprehensive documentation and examples demonstrating integration with visualization libraries like d3po.

top_posts.title: Spaghetti Code Dieting Tips
top_posts.summary: The majority of my work is about solving novel problems faced by clients. The ad-hoc nature of each project has sometimes meant past projects were organized in an ad- hoc fashion. Giles Dickenson-Jones has found it handy to try and organize analysis across sections designed to correspond with the typical steps of an analysis project.

top_posts.title: Text analysis of 2024 US Presidential convention speeches
top_posts.summary: The post discusses a numerical text analysis of the 2024 US Presidential convention speeches by Trump and Harris. Using R packages like tm and tidytext, the analysis includes sentiment analysis, word frequency, and other textual statistics. It highlights that Trump's speech has a higher percentage of negative words and anger-related sentiments compared to Harris. However, the overall emotion distribution of their speeches is surprisingly similar.

top_posts.title: How to Apply AI to Small Data Sets?
top_posts.summary: As more companies and manufacturers use AI in their manufacturing processes, data availability is dwindling. The SSL model is mostly employed for classification and regression analysis activities. It is also useful for categorizing unlabeled data. As it constructs and manages the entire process separately, this model has quickly resolved the data labeling difficulty.
